sections.COMMENTS:
ï»¿    **COMMENTS**
The domain of active strike-slip deformation in NW and W Slovenia is positioned between the S vergent thrust domain in the Friuli area of NE Italy and SW thrusting domain of the Dinarides. Earthquake and geology data in NE Italy indicate that the prevailing mechanism of deformation is thrusting on E-W oriented planes whereas dextral-reverse and purely dextral strike-slip displacements on NNW-SSE oriented planes occur further E and SE. The prevailing fault orientation in the Dinarides is in the orogen-parallel NW-SE direction. Earthquakes and geologic data along these faults exhibit thrust focal mechanisms in the southern and central parts of the Dinarides, and dextral-reverse mechanisms in the northern Dinarides.
The first stage of mountain building connected to the South Alpine orogeny is Eocene thrusting and reverse fault movements along the NE Adriatic margin. During the Eocene to Lower Miocene, NE-SW directed shortening led to thrusting and uplift along SW vergent NW-SE oriented faults in the Central and External Dinarides (e.g. Tari and Pamic, 1998; Pamic et al., 2002), Julian and Friuli Alps, and E Dolomites (Doglioni, 1987). The Eocene Dinaric faults were strongly dismembered by younger, mostly late Oligocene and Miocene, south-vergent South-Alpine thrusts and steep reverse faults, which resulted in overthrusting and refolding of Dinaric structures both in the Friuli region (Doglioni, 1987; Nussbaum, 2000) and in the Julian Alps (Placer and Car, 1998). During Late Oligocene-Miocene South Alpine shortening resulted in formation of E-W oriented thrust and reverse faults. During the Mioceneâ€“Pliocene transition, the Alpine region was subjected to a change in regional style of deformation probably due to termination of subduction and slab pull along the eastern edge of the Carpathians (Horvath and Cloetingh, 1996). This change in the regional stress field coupled with the continuous northward motion of Adria resulted in inversion and reactivation of previous favourably oriented structures. The NW-SE oriented faults were reactivated in a dextral strike-slip manner and continue to exhibit such kinematics with the ongoing deformation of 2mm/yr towards NNE oriented horizontal velocy vectors recorded by GPS measurements (Grenerczy, 2002).
The majority of regional seismicity is concentrated on N and E margins of the Adria and the region of W Julian Alps together with Friuli-Venezia Giulia, represents seismically most active area in the entire Alpine region. The NWâ€“SE oriented Idrija Fault is responsible for the strongest event recorded in the region that occured on March 26th 1511, as well as the M 5.8 event of January 1st 1926. The NWâ€“SE oriented Ravne Fault has hosted moderate sized earthquakes in 1998 and 2004 with magnitude values of 5.7 and 5.2 respectivately, while a E-W oriented thrust fault hosted the May 6th 1976 M 6.5 Friuli earthquake.
This Source lies on the SE part of the RaÅ¡a Fault. At its NW end the Source reaches the area of the regional change in the strike style, where the dominating orientation of NW-SE direction becomes more oblique and oriented in E-W sense. The same kind of trend is also observable in the direction of lithological and stratigraphic units in the area, where the Paleocene-Eocene limestones and Eocene flysch units change their regional space position from NW-SE direction at the SE end to E-W oriented exposures at the NW end of the source boundary. According to historical and instrumental eathhquake data seismicity is mainly distributed at the SE part of this Source around the Ilirska Bistrica area with seismic deformation releasing in predominantly dextral strike-slip kinematics (Pondrelli et al., 2006).
We set the depth interval of this Source based on data of local and regional geologic setting. We have obtained the average strike of this Source based on geologic maps (Buser, 1973) and field and geomorphological observations. Average dip and rake of the source were inferred from published work on local geologic conditions (Buser, 1973). Values of minimum and maximum slip rates were based on considering measured horizontal velocity vectors obtained from GPS measurements (Grenerczy et al., 2005) and considering geometrical characteristics of the source. Maximum magnitude of the source was assigned taking into consideration regional geologic conditions and seismologic data.

pictures.t: Geological map of central western Slovenia
pictures.c: Geological map of  the central part of western Slovenia showing the change in the trend of the structures and lithological and stratigraphic units from NW-SE orientation at the SE to E-W trend at the NW part ot the area covered (after Buser [1973]).

pictures.t: Map of focal mechanism solutions for the Southern Alps
pictures.c: Focal mechanism solutions for the seismic events registrated in the region of Southern Alps. Area of Branik-Ilirska Bistrica seismogenic source is characterised by dextral strike-slip kinematics on subvertical NW-SE oriented fault planes (after Pondrelli et al. [2006]).

pictures.t: Recorded historical and instrumental seismicity for the region of NE Italy and W Slovenia
pictures.c: Recorded historical and instrumental seismicity for northeastern Italy and western Slovenia. The  northwestern reach of the Idrija Fault is shown with (a). Not much seismic activity is recorded along the trace of the fault in addition to the 1511 earthquake, that is generally associated with it (after Burrato et al. [2008]).

pictures.t: Regional cross-sections across the Po Plain and the northern Adriatic Sea
pictures.c: Interpreted regional seismic reflection profiles straddling the full extents of the Adriatic basin, including the Po Plain and the adjacent Northern Apennines (to the west), Southern Alps (to the north), and Dinarides (to the east) (from Fantoni and Franciosi [2009]).
